title: Director, Corporate Counsel
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. #LI-JC2 #LI-REMOTE About the Role We’re looking to recruit a US-based Director, Corporate Legal into the Veeam Legal team. The successful candidate will lead and provide hands-on legal support on a broad range of corporate matters, with responsibility for corporate governance, corporate entity structure, mergers & acquisitions, equity plans, and strategic financing transactions including credit agreements, debt financings, and equity financings. This role also requires public company experience, including supporting U.S. securities law compliance and the preparation and review of SEC filings. You will work directly with the existing legal team and internal clients, and you must have strong interpersonal skills in order to manage internal teams and cross-functional support, and both external, and opposing counsel. What You’ll Do Provide legal counsel on corporate governance matters, including board and committee practices, corporate policies, delegation of authority, and corporate formalities. Prepare and review board and committee materials, resolutions, consents, minutes, and related governance documentation; support the corporate secretarial function and governance recordkeeping. Oversee global legal entity structure and corporate housekeeping, including formations, dissolutions, reorganizations, and ongoing maintenance in coordination with Finance and Tax. Lead and manage legal workstreams for mergers & acquisitions and other strategic transactions, including structuring, due diligence, negotiation of definitive documents, and integration support. Draft, review and negotiate key transaction documents, including LOIs, purchase agreements, disclosure schedules, and ancillary agreements. Provide legal support for equity plans and equity-related corporate matters, including plan documentation, amendments, governance approvals, and coordination with HR/Total Rewards and Finance on equity administration support. Provide legal support for credit agreements and other financing arrangements, including negotiation and review of credit facilities, guarantees, security documents, and related closing deliverables. Support debt and equity financing transactions, including term sheets, diligence, negotiation of definitive documentation, and closing execution in partnership with Treasury/Finance and external counsel. Provide public company legal support, including advising on disclosure considerations and drafting/reviewing SEC filings such as Forms 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K and proxy materials (as applicable), in coordination with Finance, Investor Relations, and external counsel. Partner with internal stakeholders on disclosure controls, governance processes, and transaction-related communications and approvals. Maintain relationships with outside counsel; manage external counsel effectively to ensure high-quality advice and cost-effective support. Manage responding to queries in a timely manner and be able to accurately direct non legal queries to the relevant department. Develop and deliver trainings for employees and executives on a variety of subjects within counsel’s areas of responsibility. What You’ll Bring Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited U.S. law school and active license to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction (in good standing). 8-12 years’ experience as an attorney with a mix of significant law firm and in-house experience, including meaningful corporate and transactional experience. Demonstrated experience with corporate governance and entity management, including preparing corporate approvals and maintaining corporate records. Significant experience leading and executing mergers & acquisitions and other complex corporate transactions. Experience supporting equity plans and equity-related corporate matters; familiarity with working cross-functionally with HR/Total Rewards and Finance. Experience advising on and negotiating credit agreements and financing transactions, including debt and/or equity financings. Public company experience required, including hands-on involvement with SEC reporting and disclosure (e.g., 10-K/10-Q/8-K and proxy materials, as applicable) and familiarity with disclosure controls and related governance requirements. Tactful with strong external and internal negotiation and conflict resolution skills. Exercise meticulous attention to detail and an organized approach to quickly identify problems and provide solutions. Ability to be creative and flexible but with a focus on business-oriented outcomes. Commercial acumen is essential. Highly developed written and oral communications skills, with the ability to clearly articulate recommendations and options about complex legal issues. Highly collaborative and able to organize and manage projects with multiple stakeholders. What you'll get Unlimited paid time off, 12 paid holidays including 4 global VeeaMe Days for self-care and 24 paid volunteer hours annually through Veeam Cares Paid parental leave: 8 weeks for all parents, 16 weeks for birthing parents Medical, dental, and vision coverage starting on your first day Mental health support, therapy sessions, and digital wellness tools via our Employee Assistance Program 401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions Fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support through Maven, plus paid volunteer time AirVet: 24/7 virtual veterinary care at no cost Legal services, identity protection, and supplemental health insurance options Tax-advantaged spending accounts for healthcare, dependent care, and commuting Opportunities to learn and grow through on-demand libraries (LinkedIn Learning, O’Reilly), mentoring, workshops, and learning events like our annual Global Day of Learning Compensation Transparency Veeam is committed to pay transparency and equitable compensation. For this role, the compensation range below reflects the expected total target compensation (TTC), inclusive of base pay and a competitive performance-based bonus. For roles with a commission plan, the compensation range represents On Target Earnings (OTE), which includes base salary plus variable commission. When determining compensation, Veeam takes into consideration factors such as experience, education, skills, and geographic zone. Offers are typically made below the midpoint of the range. In addition to compensation, Veeam provides a comprehensive benefits package, including health coverage, retirement plans, and unlimited time off. title: Director, Litigation and Regulatory
description: About Sezzle: With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We're not just transforming payments; we're redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we're building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you're excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! About the Role:  Sezzle is a publicly traded consumer finance company (Nasdaq: SEZL) building purchase-now-pay-later products for consumers who are underserved by traditional credit, and we are pursuing a de novo national bank charter. That combination puts us in front of regulators, plaintiffs' counsel, and state enforcement authorities more often than a company our size would normally be, and we handle almost all of it in-house.  This role is for a lawyer who wants to own that work rather than route it. You will run litigation and pre-litigation disputes, manage regulatory inquiries and investigations from federal and state authorities, and serve as the legal owner of our privacy and data protection framework. You will have real autonomy on day one, direct access to the executive team, and the budget discipline of a lean function that brings in outside counsel deliberately rather than reflexively. What You'll Do: Litigation and disputes Manage consumer litigation, class actions, arbitrations, and commercial disputes from intake through resolution, including case strategy, discovery, and settlement posture. Direct outside counsel where we use it: scope, budget, staffing, and strategy. You set the plan; they execute it. Own litigation holds, ESI protocols, custodian identification, and the discovery process end to end. Manage the small-claims and arbitration pipeline, and build the process improvements that keep volume from becoming a drag. Identify the patterns behind repeat disputes and take them back to product, operations, and collections so the underlying problem gets fixed. Regulatory inquiries and investigations Manage civil investigative demands, examination requests, subpoenas, and informal inquiries from the CFPB, FTC, state attorneys general, and state financial regulators. Run productions: scope negotiation, data collection, privilege review, and delivery, working with engineering, data, and compliance. Draft response letters, white papers, and advocacy submissions, and participate directly in regulator meetings. Track the enforcement and supervisory landscape across BNPL, UDAAP, credit reporting, debt collection, and consumer disclosure, and translate it into concrete guidance for the business. Support supervisory readiness as we build toward bank charter approval and the examination posture that follows. Privacy and data protection Serve as legal owner of the privacy framework: policies, notices, records of processing, data mapping, and retention. Advise on state comprehensive privacy laws, GLBA, FCRA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, and the pixel and session-replay wiretap theories that continue to generate demand letters and class actions. Review vendor and partner data flows, negotiate data protection terms, and handle escalated consumer privacy rights requests. Partner with the Chief Compliance and Privacy Officer on incident response and on the operational privacy program. AI and how the function scales Use AI to multiply your own throughput across research, document review, discovery, production, drafting, and regulatory tracking, and keep pushing what that stack can do. Build durable tooling, not one-off prompts: skills, workflows, templates, and automations that outlive the matter they were built for and that the rest of the team can run. Champion responsible AI adoption across the company. Legal is a builder here, not a brake. You will help business teams find ways to use these tools well and help set the guardrails that make that possible. Advise on AI governance as a legal matter: model use, vendor diligence, data handling, disclosure, and the emerging regulatory picture. Advisory and cross-functional Counsel product, marketing, engineering, and collections on live questions with practical answers, not memos that end in “it depends.” Build the playbooks, templates, and internal training that let the function scale without adding headcount. What We Look For: Bachelor's degree from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing in at least one US jurisdiction. You will need to satisfy in-house counsel

title: Senior Product Manager (Data Governance Platform)
description: We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time. Product Manager AI adoption across the organization is accelerating, and existing governance processes can add cycle time and rely heavily on manual review. We are building an AI Governance Engineering capability to modernize governance through automation—shifting from approval-heavy workflows to registration-driven workflows with built-in controls, and continuous observability. As a product manager in AI Governance team, you will be responsible for managing the vision, roadmap and requirements for the engineering team delivering governance-as-code roadmap: platform-agnostic SDKs, APIs, and automated controls that help teams move faster while ensuring responsible AI guardrails are consistently enforced. This role is a combination of product manager and product owner roles where you will need to operate at both 10000 ft as well as ground level providing granular requirements that team can execute on. Responsibilities Define product strategy, capabilities, and roadmaps for the governance as code team of engineers. Define Agent to agent workflows Research industry practices in this domain and choose best bath forward taking an agile approach to development Establish shared vision across the company by building consensus on priorities. Building influential relationships with business partners, stakeholders, and peer group to drive outcomes. Meet with internal stakeholders, exhibitors, and buyers to gather requirements, understand customer needs, and define product features Conducting thorough business case and value analysis to prioritize scope and approach of solutions Work with other Product Mangers and Product Owners to determine and manage cross-team dependencies. Define and analyze metrics that inform the success of our platform and related products. Following human centered thinking to design, develop and facilitate working sessions to compile business needs and user feedback. Review epics and refine user stories with the Engineering to support the development process Coordinate with the UI/UX team to define short and long-term goals and produce actionable artifacts. Maintain accurate and actionable user stories throughout the development life cycle in the new era of agentic development Verify stories are completely based on acceptance criteria. Learn and master industry knowledge and product management skills by staying curious in nature and continuously learning. Participate in the incident management process as required to support overall issue resolution. Identifying, managing, and mitigating risks at program and product level and communicate to appropriate stakeholders. Participate in Agile ceremonies such as stand ups, sprint demos, and retrospectives Identify and build relationships with key users to establish a regular cadence of feedback gathering. Exceptional soft skills, including the ability to articulate to both technical and business audiences. Excellent organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills and demonstrated experience in using tools such as Excel, Visio, Miro, PowerPoint. Minimum Qualifications: 7+ years of experience as a Product Manager working in a large, matrixed organization with many internal partners. 5+ years of experience working in an Agile methodology, using Agile productivity tools, leading incremental software releases. 5+ years of experience working on data and analytics-based platform capabilities, services, or products. 3+ years of experience working with UI/UX teams to develop wireframes and working prototypes based on end user feedback and human centered design. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with Responsible AI concepts such as fairness, transparency, explainability, and auditability. Background working in regulated or high-trust technology environments. Ability to translate governance or risk requirements into scalable solutions Education Undergraduate degree required Graduate degree preferred Preference given to candidates with degrees and credentials in agile, product management, data and analytics related fields What Success Looks Like AI intake processes are simpler, faster, and largely automated. Engineering teams have reusable SDKs and templates that make responsible AI the default. Validation of controls shifts from self-reporting to automated checks and evidence. Centralized observability provides real-time insight into AI usage, performance, and risk.
